title: AskNature
description: Documented public biomimicry knowledge base (Biomimicry Institute) for the Cross-Domain Invention Synthesizer capability area.
body:
AskNature is a documented biomimicry knowledge base from Biomimicry Institute. The leading open database of biological strategies organized by engineering function (e.g. 'manage impact', 'move in fluids'), used to seed cross-domain invention from nature.

How it works: It works by tokenizing the query and scoring each knowledge-base row on term overlap, returning the match count and top hits.

Documented uses of this capability area include corporate innovation programs, patent landscaping for R&D strategy, open-innovation challenges, and systematic inventive-problem-solving training.

title: TRIZ (Altshuller method)
description: Documented public inventive problem-solving method (Genrich Altshuller (method); tools by multiple vendors) for the Cross-Domain Invention Synthesizer capability area.
body:
TRIZ (Altshuller method) is a documented inventive problem-solving method from Genrich Altshuller (method); tools by multiple vendors. The theory of inventive problem solving derived from patent analysis: 40 inventive principles and a contradiction matrix that maps engineering trade-offs to proven solution patterns.

How it works: It works by mapping the engineering contradiction (what improves vs. what worsens) onto a matrix of inventive principles distilled from patent analysis, returning the principles that historically resolved that trade-off.

Documented uses of this capability area include corporate innovation programs, patent landscaping for R&D strategy, open-innovation challenges, and systematic inventive-problem-solving training.

title: PatSnap
description: Documented public patent intelligence platform (PatSnap) for the Cross-Domain Invention Synthesizer capability area.
body:
PatSnap is a documented patent intelligence platform from PatSnap. AI-assisted patent search and analytics platform used for landscaping, whitespace analysis, and finding cross-domain technology combinations worth inventing around.

How it works: It works by tokenizing the query and each document, computing Jaccard similarity over term sets, and ranking the archive so the closest prior art surfaces first.

title: Systematic inventive thinking
description: Documented public structured creativity method (academic method (Goldenberg, Mazursky)) for the Cross-Domain Invention Synthesizer capability area.
body:
Systematic inventive thinking is a documented structured creativity method from academic method (Goldenberg, Mazursky). A template-based method (subtraction, multiplication, division, task unification, attribute dependency) for generating inventions by structured manipulation of existing products.

How it works: It works by generating a pool of candidate ideas against the stated objective, scoring each on novelty and feasibility with a seeded evaluator, and ranking the pool so the strongest candidates surface first.
